title: Computational modeling establishes mechanotransduction as a potent modulator of the mammalian circadian clock.
one_liner_zh: 该文构建整合机械传导与昼夜节律通路的计算模型，涉及转录调控因子YAP/TAZ和MRTF的核转位，但未聚焦蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，方法为系统动力学模拟而非AI或分子模拟，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: Mechanotransduction, which is the integration of mechanical signals from the external environment of a cell to changes in intracellular signaling, governs many cellular functions. Recent studies have shown that the mechanical state of the cell is also coupled to the cellular circadian clock. To investigate possible interactions between circadian rhythms and cellular mechanotransduction, we have developed a computational model that integrates the two pathways. We postulated that translocation of the transcriptional regulators MRTF (herein referring to both MRTF-A and MRTF-B), YAP and TAZ (also known as YAP1 and WWTR1, respectively; collectively denoted YAP/TAZ) into the nucleus leads to altered expression of circadian proteins. Simulations from our model predict that lower levels of cytoskeletal activity are associated with longer circadian oscillation periods and higher oscillation amplitudes, which is consistent with recent experimental observations. Furthermore, accumulation of YAP/TAZ and MRTF in the nucleus causes circadian oscillations to decay in our model. These effects hold both at the single-cell level and within a population-level framework. Finally, we investigated the effects of mutations in YAP or lamin A, the latter of which result in a class of diseases known as laminopathies. In silico, oscillations in circadian proteins are substantially weaker in populations of cells with mutations in YAP or lamin A, suggesting that defects in mechanotransduction can disrupt the circadian clock in certain disease states; however, reducing substrate stiffness in the model restores normal oscillatory behavior, suggesting a possible compensatory mechanism. Thus, our study identifies that mechanotransduction could be a potent modulatory cue for cellular clocks and that this crosstalk can be leveraged to rescue the circadian clock in disease states.
abstract_zh: 机械转导（mechanotransduction），即细胞将外部环境的机械信号整合为细胞内信号变化的过程，调控着许多细胞功能。近期研究表明，细胞的机械状态也与细胞昼夜节律相耦合。为了探究昼夜节律与细胞机械转导之间可能的相互作用，我们开发了一个整合这两条通路的计算模型。我们假设转录调控因子MRTF（此处指MRTF-A和MRTF-B）、YAP和TAZ（分别也称为YAP1和WWTR1；统称为YAP/TAZ）向细胞核的转位会导致昼夜节律蛋白表达的改变。我们模型的模拟预测，较低的细胞骨架活动水平与较长的昼夜节律振荡周期和较高的振荡幅度相关，这与近期的实验观察一致。此外，在我们的模型中，YAP/TAZ和MRTF在细胞核中的积累会导致昼夜节律振荡衰减。这些效应在单细胞水平和群体水平框架内均成立。最后，我们研究了YAP或核纤层蛋白A（lamin A）突变的影响，后者导致一类称为核纤层蛋白病（laminopathies）的疾病。在计算机模拟中，携带YAP或核纤层蛋白A突变的细胞群体中，昼夜节律蛋白的振荡显著减弱，这表明机械转导缺陷可能在某些疾病状态下扰乱昼夜节律；然而，在模型中降低基底刚度可恢复正常的振荡行为，提示存在一种可能的补偿机制。因此，我们的研究指出，机械转导可能是细胞时钟的强效调节线索，且这种串扰可用于在疾病状态下拯救昼夜节律。
